title: The Lighthouse Keeper
logline: An ageing keeper turns a lighthouse lens by hand through a blackout storm so that eleven men she will never meet can find harbour.
setting_summary: Corrow Point, a remote island lighthouse, across forty-one winters and culminating in one blacked-out night storm.

characters.name: Mara Halloran
characters.description_from_text: Kept the light on Corrow Point for forty-one winters; seventy-three in the year of the blackout; writes the weather in a ledger nobody reads.
characters.first_mention_excerpt: For forty-one winters, Mara Halloran kept the light on Corrow Point burning.

characters.name: The captain of the Bright Endeavour
characters.description_from_text: Steered by a light that swung strangely, slower than it should, but never stopped.
characters.first_mention_excerpt: Their captain said afterwards that he had steered by a light that swung strangely.

characters.name: The interviewer
characters.description_from_text: A girl who came to interview her after the medal.
characters.first_mention_excerpt: she told the girl who came to interview her that the medal had it wrong

locations.name: Corrow Point lighthouse
locations.description_from_text: Two hundred and eleven steps to the lamp room; a clockwork lens; a kitchen with one electric bulb.

locations.name: The sea off Corrow Point
locations.description_from_text: Flat grey in August, black and hammering in February, strange green calm before the worst.

locations.name: A hall in the town
locations.description_from_text: Where they gave her a medal the following spring.

beats.summary: Mara has kept the light for forty-one winters, unasked.
beats.source_excerpt: in all that time nobody ever asked her to

beats.summary: She learns the sea's moods like a language.
beats.source_excerpt: the flat grey patience of August, the black hammering of February

beats.summary: Her routine: the wick, the clockwork, a ledger nobody reads.
beats.source_excerpt: She wrote the weather in a ledger nobody read

beats.summary: At seventy-three, the island loses all power.
beats.source_excerpt: In the winter she turned seventy-three, the light went out.

beats.summary: She understands the ships cannot see her.
beats.source_excerpt: the ships out there could not see her

beats.summary: She climbs 211 steps in the dark with oil and matches.
beats.source_excerpt: Two hundred and eleven steps with a can of oil and a box of matches

beats.summary: She lights the old lamp by hand, as the first keeper did in 1868.
beats.source_excerpt: the way the first keeper had in 1868

beats.summary: She turns the lens with her own arms all night.
beats.source_excerpt: turning the lens with her own arms because the clockwork needed power she did not have

beats.summary: Her shoulders give out near four; she keeps turning, counting aloud.
beats.source_excerpt: counting rotations aloud to stay awake

beats.summary: The Bright Endeavour makes harbour at seven with eleven men.
beats.source_excerpt: The trawler Bright Endeavour made harbour at seven. Eleven men aboard.

beats.summary: A medal in spring, which she says has it wrong.
beats.source_excerpt: the medal had it wrong. It was not brave, she said.

beats.summary: She had simply never considered letting it go out.
beats.source_excerpt: She had simply never considered letting it go out.
